blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Networking events in the UK are relaxed but important. People meet over drinks after work, at conferences, or at small breakfast meetings. Conversations are often light at first — the weather, the traffic, the weekend — before anything serious.

Business cards are still used, but most people connect on LinkedIn a day later with a short, polite message. Following up quickly and then leaving space is the British way. "Lovely to meet you — let's keep in touch."

Patience, warmth and small follow-ups beat aggressive selling every time.

items.q: Where do people meet at UK networking events?
options: At drinks, conferences and breakfast meetings
items.why: "People meet over drinks after work, at conferences, or at small breakfast meetings."

items.q: What do people often talk about first?
options: Light topics like the weather and the weekend
items.why: "Conversations are often light at first — the weather, the traffic, the weekend."

items.q: How do most people connect after the event?
options: They send a business card by post
They connect on LinkedIn a day later
They never contact each other again
items.why: "most people connect on LinkedIn a day later with a short, polite message."

items.q: The text suggests that in the UK, aggressive selling is…
options: the best way to win business
the fastest way to close a deal
less effective than warmth and patience
items.why: Inferência: "Patience, warmth and small follow-ups beat aggressive selling every time."

items.q: The phrase "leaving space" suggests that after you follow up, you should…
options: not push too hard or too fast
ask for a meeting at once
items.why: Inferência: "Following up quickly and then leaving space" — dar espaço é não pressionar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Emily falando com uma colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, I'm still buzzing after the drinks last night! It was a great evening. There were about fifty people there, and I'm following up with five of them today.

First, there was a woman from a big bank. She gave me her business card, but I'm connecting with her on LinkedIn right now. I'm writing a short, polite note — just "Lovely to meet you, let's keep in touch." Nothing pushy.

Then there was a man who runs a small tech company. We only talked about the football and the weather, honestly! But he was very warm, so I want to stay in touch.

I'm meeting one of them again next week for a quick breakfast. The other two, I'm just sending a friendly message today, and then I'm leaving them some space. I'm not chasing anyone. In the UK, that never works.

Small, kind follow-ups — that's how you build a real network here. I'm learning that slowly!
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many people is Emily following up with today?
items.why: "I'm following up with five of them today."

items.q: What is Emily doing with the woman from the bank right now?
items.why: "I'm connecting with her on LinkedIn right now."

items.q: What did Emily talk about with the man from the tech company?
items.why: "We only talked about the football and the weather, honestly!"

items.q: Why is Emily NOT sending many messages to the other two people?
options: She wants to leave them space and not chase them
items.why: Inferência: "I'm leaving them some space. I'm not chasing anyone. In the UK, that never works."

items.q: How does Emily feel about the evening?
items.why: Inferência: "I'm still buzzing… It was a great evening" — ela está animada e feliz.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "I met ten new people at the networking event." Networking is…
options: meeting people to build work contacts
items.why: Networking = fazer contatos profissionais, conhecer pessoas para o trabalho.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She gave me her ___ so I could send her an email later."
items.why: Business card = cartão de visita, com nome e contato.

items.q: "I will follow up tomorrow with a short message." To follow up means to…
options: contact again after a first meeting
items.why: To follow up = dar continuidade, entrar em contato de novo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "His ___ made me feel welcome; he was so kind and friendly."
items.why: Warmth = cordialidade, calor humano, ser gentil e acolhedor.

items.q: "Let's keep in touch!" This means…
items.why: To keep in touch = manter contato ao longo do tempo.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em networking e negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Let's catch up over coffee next week." To catch up means to…
options: meet and talk to share news
items.why: Catch up = se encontrar e conversar, colocar o papo em dia.

items.q: "I'll reach out to her on LinkedIn tomorrow." To reach out means to…
items.why: Reach out = entrar em contato, iniciar a conversa com alguém.

items.q: "Don't chase people too much after an event." To chase someone here means to…
options: run after them in the street
contact them again and again in a pushy way
items.why: Chase = ficar em cima, cobrar resposta insistentemente.

items.q: "It was lovely to meet up with the team last night." To meet up means to…
items.why: Meet up = encontrar-se pessoalmente, reunir-se.

items.q: "I need to drop her a line to say thank you." To drop someone a line means to…
items.why: Drop someone a line = mandar uma mensagem curta, dar um alô.
